market_name: Will OpenAI’s market cap be between $750B and $1T at market close on IPO day?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether any OpenAI IPO/funding headline is driving the market; if none, treat as noise.
time_plan.1h: Compare MSFT move vs. broad tech (QQQ) to isolate any OpenAI-specific signal.
time_plan.2h: Look for corroborating reporting on IPO timing or valuation; absent that, hold unclear.
time_plan.6h: Reassess whether prediction-market move persisted or reverted; a revert confirms noise.
time_plan.12h: Close research: log whether MSFT diverged from tech peers in any way tied to OpenAI news.

predictions.reasoning: Microsoft holds a large stake in OpenAI, so an OpenAI IPO valuation is economically relevant to MSFT. But this market resolves on a specific $750B-$1T bracket at some future IPO (possibly no IPO before end-2026), so any short-term probability move carries almost no clean, time-bound information for MSFT over a 12h window. A higher implied valuation could be mildly positive (mark-to-market of stake) but the bracket structure means an increase in this specific bracket's odds is ambiguous (could reflect a lower valuation ceiling vs. higher-bracket outcomes). Mapping is weak and dominated by AI-sector macro noise.

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Scan for OpenAI valuation/IPO news that would move AI sentiment broadly.
time_plan.1h: Check NVDA and SMH vs. SPX to see if any AI-specific bid is present.
time_plan.2h: Confirm whether prediction-market shift coincides with a real catalyst.
time_plan.6h: Evaluate persistence; fade the thesis if move is isolated to the prediction market.
time_plan.12h: Record outcome and whether the bracket move had any measurable SMH correlation.

predictions.reasoning: A sharply higher implied OpenAI IPO valuation would signal robust AI-capex and demand sentiment, which correlates with semiconductor names (Nvidia-heavy SMH). However, the bracket-specific and long-dated nature of this market makes it an extremely noisy sensor; a move in the $750B-$1T bracket odds does not directionally map to AI enthusiasm because it competes with both lower and higher valuation brackets. Weak proxy exposure, low confidence.

evidence_used: Market question concerns OpenAI IPO market-cap bracket ($750B-$1T) with resolution possibly as late as Dec 31, 2026
OpenAI is privately held; Microsoft is its largest strategic investor
OpenAI valuation is a barometer of AI-sector capex and sentiment affecting semiconductors
No liquid instrument directly tracks OpenAI's private valuation
uncertainty_notes: Long/undefined event horizon (up to end-2026) makes a 12h asset mapping essentially meaningless
Bracket-specific resolution means probability shifts are directionally ambiguous
Any real IPO/valuation news would already be public and priced, eliminating leakage edge
MSFT and SMH exposures are indirect and dominated by unrelated macro drivers

llm_justification.summary: This market prices a narrow OpenAI IPO market-cap bracket with an event horizon extending to end-2026, so it provides no clean, time-bound signal for any liquid asset over a 12h window. The only economically linked public proxies are Microsoft (largest OpenAI stakeholder) and AI/semiconductor ETFs, but both mappings are weak: the bracket structure makes probability moves directionally ambiguous, and any genuine IPO news would be public and already priced. Direction is unclear with low confidence; not tradable.
key_assumptions: OpenAI remains private with Microsoft as major stakeholder
No imminent IPO catalyst within the 12h window
Prediction-market moves here are dominated by speculation, not leaked information
failure_modes: An actual OpenAI IPO announcement could make this a real, public catalyst — but then it is already public, not leaked
Bracket-based odds shift could reflect a LOWER expected valuation (odds moving away from higher brackets), inverting the assumed positive read for MSFT/SMH
Microsoft and SMH are only weakly exposed; sector macro moves would swamp any OpenAI-specific effect
The market may simply resolve 'No IPO by Dec 31, 2026,' making valuation-bracket odds economically irrelevant to near-term prices
